business: Benaka, Inc. — general contractor, 7 Lawrence Street, New Brunswick, NJ (founded 1994; federal design-build, IDIQ/MACC and JOC work for Air Force, Army, Navy, DoL and the Smithsonian)
opportunity: Audit opportunity #1 — a federal QC documentation agent that drafts daily production reports, three-phase control checklists, preparatory/QC meeting minutes, RFIs and a submittal register for USACE/Air Force task orders, with the QC Manager signing every document

problem.summary: Benaka's one publicly advertised field role is a Quality Control Manager whose job description is almost a list of documents: manage the three phases of control and all associated report forms, run preparatory meetings and initial inspections, keep QC/production meeting minutes, write RFIs with the PM, prepare purchase orders, and complete daily production reports — using QCS/RMS plus Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and Project. The company is hiring that role externally at $100,000-$140,000 (and has advertised a combined 'QC Manager/Project Superintendent' posting), which points to thin field staffing carrying a heavy, continuous paperwork load across concurrent task orders inside occupied government facilities. Because the reporting spans a government system (QCS/RMS) and Office files, the same content is re-keyed or re-typed two or three times, and every document must still be performed and signed by a qualified QC Manager under the contract's QC specification. The bottleneck is drafting and reconciling, not judgement — which is what an agent can absorb while leaving classification of defects and safety conditions with the human.

current_tools.tool: USACE/Air Force QCS / RMS 3.0 Contractor Mode
current_tools.evidence: The QC Manager posting lists QCS/RMS familiarity as a plus; USACE documents QCS as 'the Contractor Module of RMS that construction contractors utilize to exchange information electronically with the Government'.

current_tools.tool: Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and Project
current_tools.evidence: The same posting requires proficiency with Office/Project and web-based programs alongside QCS/RMS, i.e. documents are produced in Office and then re-entered into the government system.

current_tools.tool: Email + fax + phone intake (Exchange/OWA at bimail.benakainc.com)
current_tools.evidence: Contact page lists phone, fax, email and a contact form, and links employee webmail to an OWA path — no portal, booking or document-exchange channel is published.

current_tools.tool: Static website with project/client galleries (no structured project data)
current_tools.evidence: Project and client history is published as flat HTML pages, so past reports, specs and photos live in files and mailboxes rather than a queryable system.

solution.design: A 'shadow' QC desk that sits beside QCS/RMS and never writes to it. Three scheduled triggers: (1) a field packet — photos plus a 2-3 minute voice note or short email — arriving in a per-project mailbox or shared folder; (2) a 4:00 pm cron per active project; (3) an inbound submittal/RFI email from the government or a subcontractor. On each trigger the agent: transcribes the voice note and captions the photos; retrieves the relevant spec section, definable feature of work (DFOW) entry and the last three approved daily reports for that project; drafts the daily production report in Benaka's own Word template with an explicit 'source' line behind every quantity and activity; maintains a submittal/RFI register in the project's Excel layout with overdue flags and age-of-review; and produces preparatory-meeting minutes and RFI drafts for the QC Manager to edit. Output always lands in a review queue as an editable Word/Excel file plus a short 'what I could not confirm' list. The QC Manager edits and signs; a human pastes or types the approved content into QCS/RMS. Nothing is emailed to a contracting officer, filed in QCS, or marked as an inspection result by the agent, and the agent never classifies a defect or a safety condition. Deployment is deliberately two-tier: the four-week pilot runs on a small self-hosted box with a commercial model API against one task order's non-sensitive documents; if the client's contract flowdowns mark any project documents as CUI/FCI, the same container is redeployed in Azure Government with Azure OpenAI, which is in FedRAMP High audit scope.

components.tool: Microsoft Graph API (Mail.Read application permission) or IMAP if the mailbox is on-premises Exchange
components.why: Field notes, government submittals and RFIs already arrive by email; reading a mailbox means the QC Manager changes no behaviour and the client buys no new channel.

components.component: Document rendering into the client's own forms
components.why: Fills Benaka's existing Word daily-report and minutes templates and Excel registers in place, so the output is the document the QC Manager already signs instead of a new format he has to retype.

components.component: Per-project retrieval (specs, DFOW list, prior reports, submittals)
components.tool: Postgres with pgvector, embeddings through the model gateway
components.why: A draft daily report is only useful if it cites the right spec section and DFOW; retrieval keeps each project's library separate and lets the agent show its source line.

components.tool: LiteLLM proxy (open source) in front of OpenAI or Azure OpenAI
components.why: Same code path for a cheap commercial model during the pilot and Azure OpenAI in Azure Government if CUI rules apply; also gives per-project token accounting and logging.
Superintendents talk faster than they type; a 3-minute voice note becomes the raw material for the report at roughly half a cent a minute.

components.component: OCR for scanned submittals and spec pages
components.why: Government submittal packages and stamped drawings arrive as scans; OCR plus layout extraction lets the register and retrieval work on them.

components.component: Review queue, sign-off and audit log
components.tool: Small self-hosted web app (FastAPI + server-rendered pages) with append-only event log
components.why: Every draft needs a visible approve/edit/reject step and a record of which source documents and which model version produced it, so the QC Manager's signature is defensible and a contracting officer's question can be answered.

integrations.method: Graph REST API, Mail.Read application permission with admin consent (scoped to a dedicated project mailbox); fall back to IMAP if the mailbox is on-premises Exchange, since the published webmail is an OWA path rather than an M365 sign-in
integrations.cost: Graph API itself is included with the tenant; a dedicated Microsoft 365 Business Basic mailbox is $6.00 per user per month on annual terms if one must be created

integrations.system: USACE/Air Force QCS — RMS 3.0 Contractor Mode
integrations.method: No public API found; USACE documentation describes QCS as the contractor module of RMS for exchanging information with the Government and provides contractor manuals/import-export help files, not a developer API. Integration therefore stays manual: agent output is re-entered or imported by the QC Manager, and the agent produces a per-document 'QCS entry checklist' instead of an automated write.
integrations.cost: Not public — QCS/RMS access is furnished through the Corps contract, not sold as a subscription (no published contractor price)

integrations.method: docxtpl/python-docx render into the client's .docx/.xlsx; openpyxl for registers
OpenAI audio transcription endpoint via LiteLLM; Azure OpenAI equivalent available for the government-cloud deployment
Azure AI Document Intelligence Read/prebuilt-layout REST API
integrations.cost: $1.50 per 1,000 pages (Read, standard pay-as-you-go; regional variation possible)

integrations.system: Azure OpenAI in Azure Government (CUI-safe path)
integrations.method: Same container redeployed against an Azure OpenAI endpoint in a US Gov region; Azure OpenAI appears in Microsoft's FedRAMP High audit scope for Azure Government
integrations.cost: Not captured — the Azure OpenAI pricing page renders per-model figures dynamically and showed placeholders on retrieval; a quote is required

solution.human_in_the_loop: The QC Manager (or PM for RFIs) is the only signer: every daily production report, minutes set, RFI and submittal transmittal is generated as a draft, reviewed in a queue, edited in Word/Excel, and signed by that person before it enters QCS/RMS or leaves the company. The agent cannot mark an inspection pass/fail, cannot classify a deficiency, cannot email a contracting officer, and cannot write to QCS. A weekly 30-minute review with the QC Manager checks rejected drafts and any 'could not confirm' flags; a monthly review with the founder checks token spend, error patterns and template drift.

steps: Pick the pilot task order and the QC Manager who will review drafts
Collect the QC plan, DFOW list, the Word daily-report and minutes templates, the Excel register, and 3 months of approved daily reports/RFIs
Read the contract's flowdown list with the PM and decide whether any pilot document is CUI/FCI (this decides VPS vs Azure Government)
Confirm whether the mailbox is Exchange on-premises or Microsoft 365 and get a dedicated read-only project mailbox approved
phases.client_provides: Named QC Manager, pilot project ID, templates and 3 months of prior documents, PM time for the CUI/flowdown call, IT approval for a scoped mailbox

steps: Build the per-project index: spec sections, DFOW list, submittal log, prior daily reports, photo library
Convert the client's Word/Excel templates into docxtpl/openpyxl templates without changing their layout
Write the source-citation layer so every drafted line carries a document/page reference or is flagged 'unconfirmed'
phases.client_provides: Digital copies of spec sections and submittals; confirmation that template layout must not change

steps: Daily production report agent: voice note + photos + tasks into the client template
Meeting-minutes agent for preparatory and QC meetings, pre-filled from the DFOW and prior minutes
RFI drafting agent that cites the spec paragraph in question and drafts the question only (no proposed answer unless asked)
Submittal/RFI register agent with overdue and age-of-review flags, plus three-phase checklist pre-fill that leaves pass/fail blank
phases.client_provides: Two or three real examples of each document type; 2 hours/week of QC Manager time for corrections

phases.phase: 3 — Review queue, logging and access control
steps: Approve/edit/reject queue with a visible diff against the draft and a 'sources used' panel
Append-only log: source document hashes, model and prompt version, editor identity, timestamp
Least-privilege access: one project mailbox, one project folder, no write access to any QCS asset; retention and deletion rules agreed with the PM
Backups and a one-page incident/rollback runbook
phases.client_provides: Who may approve, retention expectations, any IT security questionnaire

steps: Week 1: baseline timing exercise, then drafts on one project in parallel with the QC Manager's own
Weeks 2-3: daily drafts plus weekly review; log edit minutes per document and every factual correction
Week 4: run 20 back-tested RFIs and 20 daily reports against the QC Manager's versions; compute the delta and write the go/no-go memo
phases.founder_days: 5 (spread over four weeks, plus ~2 hours/week of live support)
phases.client_provides: QC Manager availability for review (est. 3-4 hours/week), field packets, access to the live project correspondence

steps: Fix the top rejection causes found in the pilot; freeze prompt and template versions
Write the runbook: what the agent drafts, what it must never do, how to correct it, escalation
Agree the monthly care scope (project additions, template changes, monthly error review) and the price
If the client opts for CUI-safe deployment, redeploy in Azure Government and re-run two weeks of documents
phases.client_provides: Decision on CUI deployment tier; sign-off on the runbook

pilot.scope: One active federal task order, four weeks, draft-only shadow mode. Deliverables: a per-project library of that task order's spec sections, DFOW list, submittals and prior reports; a working daily-production-report drafter fed by voice note/photos; preparatory and QC meeting-minutes drafting; an RFI drafter; a submittal/RFI register in the client's Excel layout with overdue flags; and a measured comparison of edit time and factual corrections against the QC Manager's own documents. Nothing is transmitted to QCS/RMS or to the Government during the pilot.
pilot.weeks: 4 weeks of pilot after a 1-2 week build; 5-6 weeks from go-ahead to pilot result
success_metrics: Median QC Manager edit time per daily report at least 40% below baseline by week 4
At least 60% of drafted documents accepted with under 10 minutes of editing in week 4
Zero factual errors in the final two weeks that would have changed the content of a signed QC record (quantities, dates, locations, spec references)
Submittal/RFI register catches every overdue item the QC Manager identifies manually, plus at least one the manual process missed
20 back-tested RFIs and 20 daily reports scored against the QC Manager's versions for spec citation accuracy and omissions
QC Manager states in writing that he would keep using it, and measured founder support load is 3 hours/week or less
pilot.baseline_method: Two-part baseline taken in week 1, before drafts are shown: (a) the QC Manager's own log of minutes spent producing each daily report, minutes set and RFI for 10 working days; (b) a timed exercise where he produces three daily reports and two RFIs from the same field packet the agent will later receive, so the delta is measured on identical inputs rather than on memory. Register baseline is a manual count of overdue submittals/RFIs he identifies from the current Excel or QCS view.
pilot.exit_criteria: Continue only if (1) the 40% edit-time reduction and the zero-material-error bar are both met, (2) the QC Manager will sign off in writing, (3) the client confirms the deployment tier is acceptable to its PM/KO for the documents involved, and (4) measured support load is under 3 hours/week. Otherwise the engagement converts to a paid diagnostic memo and stops; no monthly fee begins.

competitors.product: RMS 3.0 Contractor Mode / QCS (the incumbent system the contract already specifies)
competitors.fit_for_this_business: This is the system of record Benaka must use on Corps/Air Force work. It stores the three-phase control records but does not draft anything: the QC Manager still types the daily report, minutes and RFI text before entry, which is exactly the gap the agent fills. Any design that tries to replace it fails on contract compliance.
competitors.price: Not public — furnished through the contract rather than sold; no published contractor subscription price found

competitors.product: Procore for Government (daily logs, quality inspections, observations in a government-oriented environment)
competitors.fit_for_this_business: Closest full-suite alternative: would hold daily logs, inspections and submittals in one place and reduce re-keying. But it is a system of record to migrate into, not a drafting assistant, and Benaka would still have to satisfy QCS-formatted QC requirements and train field staff.
competitors.price: Not public — Procore's pricing page routes to a custom quote and states annual contracts; pricing varies with products and construction volume

competitors.fit_for_this_business: Cheap, credible field tool for checklists, photos and — on Business Plus — RFIs, submittals and reports. Good for the register and photo evidence; it does not write the narrative daily QC report from field notes, and the government QC forms still have to be produced.
competitors.price: Pro $39, Business $64, Business Plus $89 per user per month, billed annually (Basic free; monthly-billing prices are higher)

competitors.fit_for_this_business: Strong daily-report product that field crews actually use, with report templates and photo capture. It standardises the report but still requires a person to write it; QC-specific three-phase records and QCS formatting are not its centre.
competitors.price: Not public — the vendor's own purchasing article directs customers to sales for plan pricing and does not list a rate

competitors.product: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud — document management, submittal log, quality management, project closeout)
competitors.fit_for_this_business: Would give Benaka a structured document and submittal system with quality-management modules; heavy for a firm that must keep QCS as the record, and it does not draft the QC narrative.
competitors.price: Not public for the construction bundles — the vendor's construction pricing page routes every bundle to 'Get a Quote'

competitors.product: Federal construction QC application (three-phase control, deficiency tracking, daily reports)
competitors.fit_for_this_business: The most directly comparable vertical product: purpose-built around federal QC workflows, which is Benaka's exact requirement. Whether it drafts text from field input or only structures it is not established from public material.
competitors.price: Not public — no published price found; the site was returned as an early-access/demo request page and refused automated retrieval (HTTP 403)

competitors.product: AI document assistant for construction (spec/submittal Q&A, unlimited users)
competitors.fit_for_this_business: Would answer 'what does the spec say' questions and surface requirements quickly, which helps RFI drafting. It is a retrieval/chat layer, not a producer of the signed daily report or register, so it complements rather than replaces the proposed design.
competitors.price: Not public — priced on construction volume, quote required, unlimited users

competitors.fit_for_this_business: Adjacent, not overlapping: it reads contracts and flags risky clauses. Useful at bid stage for Section L/M risk, but it does not touch daily QC documentation.
competitors.price: Not public — vendor listing states pricing depends on use case and project volume

competitors.product: Quality Control Manager / QC Manager-Superintendent hire
competitors.fit_for_this_business: The option Benaka is actually pursuing. It solves the problem completely and carries judgement, credentials and clearance eligibility that no software has — but it costs a full salary and cannot scale across several task orders without more hires. The agent's thesis is to make one QC Manager cover more work, not to replace him.
competitors.price: Benaka's own live posting advertises $100,000-$140,000 per year for QC Manager/Project Superintendent; BLS/O*NET 2025 New Jersey wage data put Construction Managers (SOC 11-9021) at a median of $138,230 per year ($66.46/hour), with the 25th percentile at $110,230 and the New York-Newark-Jersey City metro median at $158,000

suggested_pricing.pilot_fee: $1,800 fixed for the four-week, one-task-order pilot (credited in full against the set-up fee if the client continues)
suggested_pricing.setup_fee: $3,500 one-time (net $1,700 after the pilot credit), covering the project library, template conversion, mailbox scoping, review queue and runbook
suggested_pricing.monthly_fee: $450 per month on a 12-month minimum, covering up to two active projects, template changes, monthly error review and 3 hours of support; each additional project +$150 per month
suggested_pricing.reasoning: Inference, reasoned from three anchors. (1) Value: the audit estimates $9,700-$22,600 a year in QC drafting time at $72/hour, midpoint ~$16,150; the recommended year-one total is ~$8,900 (pilot $1,800 + net set-up $1,700 + 12 × $450), which sits just below the low end of that range and about 55% of the midpoint, so the client keeps a positive first-year return even if only the conservative case is realised. (2) Competitor frame: Fieldwire Business Plus — which handles registers and RFIs but drafts nothing — is $89/user/month, i.e. ~$5,340 a year for a five-person field team, and a single QC Manager hire is $100,000-$140,000 a year; the fee has to look like a fraction of a hire and no more than a small multiple of a field app. (3) Founder economics: at ~24 founder-days for the first build, $3,500 set-up is far below cost — the first client is a product investment, and the fee only works because the same core is resold to other small federal GCs at the same $3,500/$450 shape; recurring load is ~2-3 hours/month, which puts the monthly fee at roughly $150-$225 per hour of actual care work. Guardrails: if the pilot lands under 40% edit-time reduction, drop to a $250/month register-only scope or decline the retainer; do not discount the set-up fee further without cutting scope (e.g. one project, no OCR).

leverage.point: A reusable 'federal QC document core' (mailbox intake → retrieval → Word/Excel render → review queue → audit log) that is client-agnostic; the second and third small federal GC sold the same core needs only new templates and a new project library, which is where the margin is.

The output format is the client's own Word/Excel template, so the agent rides on tools Benaka already owns and on QCS as the untouched record — no migration project, no data-migration objection, no training burden.

Public federal source material can be baked in once and reused for every client: UFGS 01 45 00 defines the three phases of control, QC plan contents and documentation the agent must mirror, and USACE contractor manuals define the QCS fields.

A single container can be redeployed from a $12/month VPS to Azure Government with Azure OpenAI, which appears in Microsoft's FedRAMP High audit scope — that same code path becomes the answer to the DFARS cloud-safeguarding question for every DoD client, rather than bespoke work each time.
Open-source components (python-docx, docxtpl, LiteLLM, Postgres/pgvector) mean near-zero software cost per client, so the monthly fee is almost entirely care and hosting margin.

Opportunity #2 in the same house (bid-desk agent) shares the past-performance index and retrieval layer; opportunity #3 shares the mailbox intake and register pattern, so a Benaka relationship compounds without a second platform.

edge_vs_competitors: Three defensible edges and two honest gaps. Edges: (1) Local presence — the founder is roughly ten minutes from 7 Lawrence Street, so a same-week walkthrough and on-site review with the QC Manager is possible in a way it is not for a national vendor; (2) QCS-compatible by design — because the agent drafts in Benaka's Word/Excel templates and treats QCS as read-only, it does not ask a firm mid-task-order to change its system of record, which is the main objection to Procore/Autodesk/Fieldwire; (3) private deployment — the same build can run in Azure Government for CUI-adjacent documents, which most construction-software vendors and every consumer AI subscription cannot offer. Gaps: there is no track record, no reference client, no security clearance and no audit history, so Benaka is being asked to be first; and the big field platforms have mobile apps, photo annotation and hundreds of integrations that this build does not. The proposal should therefore not claim to be a better Fieldwire or Procore — it is a drafting layer above them, and the pilot is the only proof offered.

risks_compliance.issue: QC documents generated under a federal contract are Federal Contract Information at minimum, so the systems that process them must meet basic safeguarding requirements.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: FAR 52.204-21, Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems (Nov 2021) — access limitation, authentication, media sanitisation and physical access controls apply to the contractor's information systems that process FCI
risks_compliance.mitigation: Run the agent in a dedicated, least-privilege environment with named users, MFA on every account, encrypted storage, no personal devices, documented sanitisation on project close-out; keep the design in the client's own tenancy or a single-tenant host rather than a shared consumer tool.

risks_compliance.issue: If any project document is Controlled Unclassified Information (covered defense information), using an external cloud or AI service to process it triggers DoD safeguarding and incident-reporting duties.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: DFARS 252.204-7012 — the contractor must implement NIST SP 800-171-equivalent safeguards, report cyber incidents to DoD, and, if using an external cloud provider to store/process/transmit covered defense information, 'require and ensure' that the provider meets security requirements equivalent to the FedRAMP Moderate baseline
risks_compliance.mitigation: Treat CUI determination as a gate in phase 0. If CUI is in scope, deploy only in Azure Government (Azure OpenAI is in FedRAMP High audit scope for Azure Government) and mirror NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 controls in the client's system security plan; never route those documents through a commercial consumer API.

risks_compliance.issue: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 is the control set the client's own SSP is assessed against, so an agent touching CUI becomes part of that assessment boundary.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations
risks_compliance.mitigation: Scope the pilot to documents the PM agrees are not CUI; if CUI is unavoidable, provide the client with the agent's component inventory, data-flow description and control mapping so it can be added to their SSP rather than appearing as an unassessed shadow system.

risks_compliance.issue: The QC Manager holds personal accountability for QC records: three-phase control, submittals, certifications and documentation are his duties under the specification, so a fluent but wrong AI draft becomes his signature.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: UFGS 01 45 00 (Quality Control) — the QC Manager 'must perform the three phases of control, perform submittal review, ensure testing is performed and provide QC certifications and documentation required by this Contract'; the three phases of control are mandatory for each definable feature of work
risks_compliance.mitigation: Draft-only mode with mandatory human edit and signature; no auto-classification of pass/fail or deficiencies; a per-line source citation or an explicit 'unconfirmed' flag; an append-only log of who edited what; a weekly review of rejected drafts so recurring errors are fixed rather than repeated.

risks_compliance.issue: Work is on military installations and the client's own QC hires are contingent on federal security clearance/background checks; the agent (and the founder) will not hold clearance.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: Benaka's QC Manager posting states employment is contingent on a federal security clearance / background check for access to military installations
risks_compliance.mitigation: Scope the engagement to unclassified administrative documents; the founder never handles classified material and does not need site access beyond an escorted visit; documents move by mailbox/folder, not by physical media, and any site visit is arranged through the PM.

risks_compliance.issue: Prompt injection or malicious content in inbound email, submittal PDFs or photos (instructions disguised as text) could make the agent take an unintended action or inject false content into a draft.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: Inference — no construction-specific rule found; the exposure follows from giving an agent read access to third-party email and attachments, which the design requires
risks_compliance.mitigation: No tool execution or outbound sending from parsed content; documents are treated as data only; outbound email is disabled in the agent; a fixed allowlist of templates and recipients; human approval is the only path to a filing, so an injected instruction can at worst produce a bad draft that is visible in the diff.

risks_compliance.issue: Photographs taken inside occupied facilities can capture workers, badges or building security features, which raises privacy and client-confidentiality questions separate from CUI.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: Inference — no specific rule confirmed for this use; Benaka's own site says work happens in fully occupied facilities with concurrent projects, which is where such photos arise
risks_compliance.mitigation: Agree a photo rule in phase 0 (no faces, no badges, no access-control detail), run a face/plate blur step before captioning, and store photos only in the project library with the same retention as the report.

risks_compliance.issue: No rule was found that specifically authorises or prohibits a contractor using generative AI to draft QC records; the safe reading is that the record must be accurate and the human must own it, not that AI drafting is banned.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: Could not confirm any DoD/USACE rule addressing AI-drafted contractor QC documentation; related DoD CUI policy and public-affairs AI guidance could not be retrieved (HTTP 403) and are not cited here as governing
risks_compliance.mitigation: Ask the PM to confirm in writing with the KO/COR that draft-only AI assistance on unclassified project documents is acceptable on the pilot task order before week 1, and keep that note in the project file.

risks_compliance.issue: Consultant liability: an error in a draft that reaches a signed record could produce a claim against a one-person side business with no insurance or capital.
risks_compliance.rule_or_source: Inference — commercial risk, not a cited rule
risks_compliance.mitigation: Written scope that the agent produces drafts only and the client's QC Manager is the author of record; a liability cap at fees paid; no warranty of accuracy; consider professional liability cover before the first retainer; keep the pilot inside an existing task order so an error is caught by the client's own QC process.

feasibility.weeks_to_pilot: 5-6 weeks from go-ahead to pilot result (1-2 weeks build, 4 weeks shadow running)
feasibility.reasoning: Technically this is a well-understood build — mailbox intake, per-project retrieval, Word/Excel rendering and a review queue — with no exotic dependency, and running costs are around $35-$40 a month, so a solo founder can ship it. The technical score is held at 3 rather than 4 because three things are unresolved: QCS/RMS has no public API, so the 'last mile' stays manual and the agent's value stops at the draft; the client's mailbox appears to be on-premises Exchange (OWA path), which may remove Microsoft Graph from the design; and the accuracy bar is unforgiving because a fluent wrong quantity lands on a QC record a human signs — retrieval and citation discipline, not model quality, is the real engineering risk. Commercially it is 3: the pain is unusually well evidenced (a public $100K-$140K job description that is essentially a document list), the client has real contract value behind it (a $134M-ceiling Air Force MACC and a 2026 USACE MATOC), and the audit's value range ($9,700-$22,600) supports a $450/month fee — but margins on federal construction are thin, the decision-maker is unnamed publicly, the first build is ~24 founder-days against a $3,500 set-up, and the sale must go through a general inbox to a firm that is simultaneously trying to hire the very person the product helps. Conditions for proceeding: (1) a written CUI/flowdown determination for the pilot task order, (2) a named QC Manager who agrees to 3-4 hours a week for four weeks, (3) acceptance that QCS entry stays manual, and (4) a pilot contract with the 40% edit-time and zero-material-error exit criteria attached. If the CUI answer requires full NIST SP 800-171 system treatment in week 1, defer to Not now — that is a two-client-scale build, not a pilot.

discovery_questions: Which active task order can we use for a four-week pilot, who is the QC Manager on it, and how many federal projects is that person covering at once?
What exactly does today's daily production report contain (fields, photos, quantities, signature block) and where does the blank template live — Word, Excel, QCS, or all three?
How long does one daily report, one set of preparatory-meeting minutes and one RFI take to produce today, and can we time ten documents to set the baseline?
Is the mailbox Microsoft 365 or on-premises Exchange, and can IT create a dedicated read-only project mailbox that the agent can access?
Have your contracting officers or CORs said anything about CUI marking, cloud services or AI use on these task orders — can the PM walk through the flowdown clauses with us?
Who signs daily reports and RFIs today, and what is the review path between the field note and the QCS entry?
Would you rather the submittal register mirror the QCS fields exactly or stay in your own Excel format?
If the pilot shows less than a 40% reduction in editing time, what would you want instead — a register-only tool, or nothing?

caveats: The impact range ($9,700-$22,600/year) is the audit's assumption-based estimate (45 weeks × 6-10 hours × 50-70% drafted at $72/hour); no Benaka time data exists, so it is a hypothesis the pilot baseline is designed to test, not a promise.

The audit and this plan assume the daily report, minutes and RFI content is the right target; if the real time sink is photograph handling, QCS data entry or submittal logging, the design has to shift after discovery.
Founder-days are inferences from building similar document pipelines, not measured on this codebase; the first client will take longer than the second.
